subject: PO stitching, invoice cadence, and tiered discount eligibility
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@pioneerhealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pioneerhealth.com, james.wu@pioneerhealth.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO / invoice cadence / discount trigger questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups before we finalize the SOW:

- Can Redwood accept a consolidated monthly invoice that references multiple POs (we call it PO stitching)? Our AP team prefers to issue separate POs per business unit but pay on a single monthly statement.
- Pioneer standard terms are Net60. Will that affect eligibility for the volume-based discounts listed in your pricing schedule? Do discounts apply on invoiced spend or collected spend?
- We need your PO template and the final SOW to route through our systems.

We have a target go-live in mid-August and want to lock commercial terms this week. I attached our internal procurement checklist as a reference.

Appreciate a quick run-through of options.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Procurement Manager, Pioneer Health Systems
(Attachment: Pioneer_Procurement_Checklist.pdf)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@pioneerhealth.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO / invoice cadence / discount trigger questions

Hi Elena — great to hear, and thanks for the checklist. Short answers below and a few options so procurement can pick the path that maps best to your systems.

1) PO stitching / consolidated monthly invoice
- Yes — we can include multiple PO references on a single monthly invoice. We surface PO numbers as invoice line metadata so your AP can reconcile by PO. One caveat: our finance team needs a stable PO-to-entity mapping for tax/GL reasons (we ask for a primary parent PO or entity code in the CSV template).

2) Net terms and discount triggers
- Our standard public terms are Net45. Discounts in the pricing schedule are triggered on invoiced spend (not contingent on cash collection). If you require Net60, that doesn’t automatically strip discounts, but it is a commercial exception — we’ll need approval from RevOps/Finance for the extended terms.

3) Docs
- Attached: Redwood_PO_Template.csv and a draft SOW (SOW_Pioneer_v2.pdf). Also attaching an early-pay term sheet that outlines a small early-pay discount if Pioneer wants to keep Net60 but accelerate payment for priority processing.

If you’re open, we can do a 20-minute alignment call with procurement + my finance counterpart (Vivek) to confirm mapping and any initial credit hold.

Next steps I suggest: pick your preferred invoice cadence (monthly consolidated vs. per-PO), confirm PO fields we should require, and I’ll route the Net60 request internally.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template.csv, SOW_Pioneer_v2.pdf, Redwood_EarlyPay_Termsheet.pdf)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: PO / invoice cadence / discount trigger questions — Pioneer (DL-2026-4291)

Forwarding procurement request from Pioneer (see below). They want: consolidated monthly invoice referencing multiple POs, Net60, and clarity that discounts apply on invoiced spend.

Quick asks for your guidance:
- Commercial: If we approve Net60 as a standard concession, what is reasonable to offer on discount structure? They’re a large account but want to preserve the published tiering.
- Finance/ops: Are we comfortable with PO stitching (multiple PO refs on one invoice) if they provide a primary parent PO or entity code in our CSV? Any caveats I should flag to procurement?

I’ve attached the docs I sent them. Planning to propose a 6-month introductory discount or an early-pay rebuttal if Net60 is approved. Thoughts?

Thanks — Aisha
(Attachment: Redwood_PO_Template.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: PO / invoice cadence / discount trigger questions — Pioneer (DL-2026-4291)

Aisha — quick take from commercial:

- Pioneer looks strategic. I’d offer a short-term concession rather than a permanent repricing shift. Proposal: 5% usage discount for the first 6 months conditioned on a committed 6-month minimum spend (we can set a $200k minimum; if they fall short, we claw back pro rata).
- Maintain published tiering after the intro period. That keeps product economics predictable.
- If Finance approves Net60 without additional credit controls, require a 30-day ramp holdback on invoices 1–2 (e.g., 20% hold until PO stitching mapping confirmed).

I like the early-pay term sheet as an option: give them Net60 but allow an early-pay 1.5% fee if they can pay Net30. Attach term sheet to this thread and mention RevOps approval required.

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
(Attachment: Redwood_EarlyPay_Termsheet.pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: PO / invoice cadence / discount trigger questions — Pioneer (DL-2026-4291)

Thanks for pulling this together. Operational guidance from Finance:

1) PO stitching
- Finance will accept multiple PO references on a single monthly invoice provided Pioneer populates the required CSV fields in our template (primary PO, business unit code, tax entity). We will not split tax reporting across invoices without a parent PO identifier.

2) Net60 request
- We can approve Net60 for Pioneer as a commercial exception, but we need either:
  a) a short initial credit assessment and 20% holdback on first two monthly invoices until reconciliation is complete, or
  b) an irrevocable pre-funded credit or initial deposit covering month one.

3) Discount mechanics
- Confirmed: discounts apply on invoiced spend (the invoice amount after any credits/adjustments). Introductory discounts (Ben’s 5% for six months) are acceptable if we document clawback terms in the MSA amendment.

Recommended next steps (I can join the call):
- A short alignment call with Pioneer procurement (Elena + James), Aisha, Ben, and me to confirm the CSV mapping and agree on the holdback approach.
- Legal to draft a 6-month amendment that includes the introductory discount, clawback language, and Net60 approval clause.

If that sounds good I’ll notify RevOps to queue the exception review and set the credit check.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: none)
